title: Why Multi-Channel Messaging Becomes More Valuable Over Time
summary: Most marketing budgets are built around a single question: what did this campaign return?
body_text: Most marketing budgets are built around a single question: what did this campaign return? It is a fair question, but it treats every message as a standalone transaction with a fixed payoff. That framing misses the fact that trust behaves less like a series of one-off returns and more like compound interest. Just as small, consistent financial deposits grow into something far larger than the sum of the contributions, small, relevant, well-timed messages across multiple channels build a store of trust that makes every future interaction more effective. A customer who has heard from you consistently and helpfully over six months is not slightly more likely to convert than a first-time contact. They are dramatically more likely. Below, we go into that dynamic as a framework we call the trust compounding curve, and show why a coordinated presence across channels beats any single channel over time. What is the trust compounding curve? The trust compounding curve is the principle that the value of each customer interaction increases non-linearly when it is part of a consistent, connected conversation across multiple channels. A single-channel campaign tends to produce a flat, predictable return. Send an email blast, get a response rate, repeat. A coordinated multi-channel strategy behaves differently. Each touchpoint raises the trust baseline, which makes the next conversion more likely and less expensive to earn. The financial analogy is exact. Deposit a small amount consistently, and returns build on prior returns rather than starting from zero each time. Messages work the same way. A helpful onboarding email makes an in-app tip land better. That in-app moment makes a later push notification feel welcome rather than intrusive. Value accumulates . There is a measurable reason trust compounds faster than raw reach. Research on the neuroscience of trust documented by Claremont Graduate University's Paul Zak found that high-trust environments produce 74% less stress, 50% higher productivity, and 76% more engagement, driven by oxytocin released when people experience consistent, credible behavior from someone they take seriously (Speakr Brand). The same dynamic plays out between a brand and its audience. As that analysis puts it, a reader who encounters a credible voice three times across six months is not three times more likely to trust it. They are far more likely, because trust compounds non-linearly. To capture that compounding, you need infrastructure built for it. A multi-channel messaging platform that unifies customer data and coordinates every channel is the foundation. Without it, each channel operates in its own silo, and the reinforcing effect never gets a chance to build. The mechanics of compounding: How multi-channel messaging builds trust Compounding starts when channels stop competing for attention and start feeding each other. When one dollar of effort does two or three jobs at once, the whole system gets more efficient. Compounding is what happens when each touchpoint makes the next one cheaper, faster, or more likely to convert, and channels compound when one strategy runs across every channel against the same buyer journey. From isolated touchpoints to a coherent conversation The old model is batch and blast: pick a channel, push the same message to everyone, measure the open rate, move on. Each send is disconnected from the last. The compounding model treats the customer relationship as one continuous conversation where context carries across channels. This matters because customers already move fluidly between channels. A coordinated strategy meets them where they choose to engage rather than forcing them down a single path. That respect for user choice is itself a trust signal. When you let people decide where and how they hear from you, the decision to stay, explore, or buy feels like their own, which is precisely how loyalty gets built over time . Reinforcing credibility at every stage of the lifecycle The compounding effect becomes clearest when you map touchpoints across the customer lifecycle. Consider a simple sequence: Onboarding: A welcome email introduces your product and sets expectations. Activation: An in-app message highlights the key feature that delivers the first real win. Retention: A push notification or SMS surfaces a time-sensitive offer or a reason to return. Each message references and builds on what came before. The result reads as a helpful guide, not a stack of disconnected ads. The starting point is knowing which milestones you want users to reach and how long each transition should take. A flight booking app might track flight searched, then price alert set, then booking, while a gaming app maps less linear milestones like account created and level five reached. Defining autonomous lifecycle marketing Autonomous lifecycle marketing is the use of AI to plan, execute, and continuously optimize every customer interaction across the full lifecycle, treating the customer journey as a single connected system rather than a set of isolated campaigns owned by different teams and tools. It connects every stage, from awareness through retention and advocacy, into one system that keeps optimizing itself. It helps to define it against the two approaches that came before. Manual campaigns are one-off, labor-intensive sends. A marketer segments an audience, writes a message, picks a time, and hits send. It works, but it does not scale, and it cannot react to what happens next. Rule-based automation , the classic drip sequence, improves on this with static if-then logic. If a user signs up, send email one. Wait three days, send email two. This is a real step forward, but the rules never change on their own. The difference with autonomous lifecycle marketing is adaptive intelligence. One useful comparison describes rule-based systems as a recipe with fixed steps, while an AI-driven system is a baker who watches the dough, adjusts for humidity, and knows exactly when each loaf is ready. AI processes interactions across your website, email engagement, purchase history, and app behavior to make autonomous decisions about what to send, when, and on which channel. Agents monitor behavior, trigger the right message at the right moment, and adapt as customers move through each stage, so campaigns scale without scaling headcount. Running this at scale depends on a few enabling conditions: unified customer data so the system has full context, multi-channel orchestration so it can act across channels, and trigger logic that responds to real-time behavior rather than a fixed calendar. The essential channels in a modern multi-channel stack A strong strategy uses each channel for what it does best rather than pushing the same message everywhere. Here is how the primary channels contribute to a compounding, trust-building relationship. Push notifications are built for timely, high-visibility moments: a status update, a re-engagement nudge, a relevant alert. Because they land directly on the device, they carry weight, which makes restraint and relevance essential. Email is the workhorse for onboarding, richer content, and less urgent communication. It gives you room for detail, and it remains the most-used outbound channel, showing a 30% increase in volume since 2022 (Forbes) [7] . It is where you build authority and explain value at length. SMS and RCS are for time-sensitive, critical messages where deliverability and immediacy matter: shipping alerts, appointment reminders, security codes. RCS extends this into richer, more conversational exchanges. These channels demand explicit opt-in, and used well, they shift the question from cost per message to the value each conversation creates ( The New ROI of Engagement ). In-app messaging reaches users at the exact moment they are engaged. It is ideal for contextual guidance, feature announcements, and collecting feedback, because the message meets someone already in your product. Live Activities keep time-sensitive updates visible on the lock screen and in real time, useful for delivery tracking, live scores, or any ongoing event a user wants to follow at a glance. The compounding effect appears when these channels operate as one automated flow rather than separate tools. A visual automation builder can send email, push, SMS, and in-app messages based on user behavior, time delays, or profile attributes, all without writing code. Platform capabilities for autonomous lifecycle marketing A multi-channel messaging platform is the engine behind everything above. Four capabilities separate a platform that can actually run autonomous lifecycle marketing from one that just sends messages. Unified user profiles. The system needs a single view of each customer that pulls data from every channel and every interaction. Without unified data, messages contradict each other and context is lost the moment a user switches channels. A user model that ties push tokens, email addresses, and phone numbers to one profile makes coordinated messaging possible. Visual workflow automation. Marketers need to build, visualize, and adjust cross-channel lifecycle flows without waiting on engineering. A journeys builder handles onboarding sequences that guide new users to their first win, re-engagement campaigns for users who have gone quiet, and abandoned cart flows that recover lost revenue. AI-powered triggers and personalization. The platform should trigger messages off real-time behavior and personalize content at scale. Using liquid syntax and custom data across channels, you can tailor delivery and content by user attributes, events, location, and language. Real-time analytics. A feedback loop closes the system. Measuring what works, then feeding those results back into the next decision, is what turns a set of campaigns into something that improves on its own. Together these form a unified orchestration hub that connects user data to automated messaging across every channel, which is what a customer engagement platform is designed to deliver. How leading platforms approach multi-channel orchestration The market has taken several routes to multi-channel engagement, and understanding the differences helps clarify what an accessible, unified approach looks like. Some platforms lead with an AI-first identity, adopting agentic and AI-autonomous framing as their primary language. These platforms have pursued acquisitions of AI personalization engines to deepen autonomous campaign capabilities and offer a purpose-built AI layer positioned above cross-channel orchestration as the intelligence layer for marketers. Others differentiate on delivery mechanics, highlighting proprietary push-delivery technology aimed at device-level notification suppression, the battery-optimization settings that can silently block notifications. Still others anchor their guidance in raw engagement data, emphasizing how push notifications can significantly increase engagement compared to users who receive no messages, across channel types spanning mobile, web, connected TV, wearables, desktop, and in-app. OneSignal takes the position that powerful multi-channel messaging and autonomous lifecycle marketing should be achievable for businesses of every size, from a solo builder launching an MVP to a global enterprise. The platform unifies six channels, push, web push, email, SMS/RCS, in-app messaging, and Live Activities, behind one user model, a visual Journeys builder, and real-time analytics, delivering more than 12 billion messages daily. Email and SMS can be set up without a developer, which keeps the barrier to a coordinated strategy low. The goal is a fast, intuitive way to run a coordinated conversation across channels rather than stitching together separate tools. Avoiding the pitfalls: How to compound trust, not annoyance Multi-channel done poorly compounds the opposite of trust. More channels mean more ways to irritate someone into leaving. The same coordination that builds credibility can erode it if the fundamentals are ignored. Here are the common failure modes and how to prevent them. Over-messaging. The fastest way to burn trust is volume without value. Use frequency capping to limit how often a single user hears from you, and lean on smart delivery timing so messages arrive when a person is actually receptive, drawing on intelligent delivery that meets users when they are most likely to engage. Channel mismatch. The right message on the wrong channel still fails. Reserve SMS for genuinely time-sensitive or transactional content that the user opted in to receive, and keep longer, less urgent material in email or in-app. Matching intent to channel is what makes each touchpoint feel considered. Inconsistent voice. Compounding depends on the customer recognizing one coherent brand across every channel. If the email sounds formal and the push sounds like a different company entirely, the accumulated trust resets each time. Keep tone, language, and design aligned so every message reinforces the last. Ignoring preferences. Make it genuinely easy for users to manage how and how often they hear from you. A clear preference center is a trust signal, because it hands control back to the customer, and the freedom to choose is exactly what makes people willing to stay engaged over the long run. Building for long-term growth The most valuable marketing outcome is not a spike from a single campaign. It is a trusted relationship that keeps returning more value the longer it runs. That is what the trust compounding curve describes: a measurable dynamic where each consistent, relevant, cross-channel touchpoint raises the probability of retention and conversion non-linearly, so multi-channel outperforms single-channel by a widening margin over months and years. Getting there takes two things. First, a strategic shift from counting impressions to designing conversations, treating the customer journey as one connected system rather than a stack of disconnected sends. Second, a unified platform capable of coordinating every channel, adapting to real behavior, and learning from its own results. Put those together, and the curve starts working in your favor, quietly, every day, compounding the trust that turns acquisition into lasting loyalty. Built to put the trust compounding curve to work. OneSignal unifies push, web push, email, SMS/RCS, in-app messaging, and Live Activities behind a single user profile, a no-code Journeys builder, and real-time analytics — so every touchpoint reinforces the last. Whether you're a solo founder running your first onboarding flow or an enterprise team orchestrating millions of messages a day, you can start building coordinated, trust-compounding conversations without stitching together a stack. What separates tools in 2026 is verification quality (how many bounce), coverage on mobile phone numbers (the hard part), and whether the data actually goes anywhere. Below we rank the field honestly, credit the specialists that beat everyone on raw data depth, and say plainly who should pick each one. The best email finder tool is Artisan, because it treats the found email as the start of the job rather than the end. Ava searches over 250M B2B professionals, runs the email through waterfall enrichment across roughly a dozen providers, verifies it, and only charges when she lands a valid address. Then she writes and sends the outreach, handles the reply, and books the meeting. A standalone finder stops at the address. If you only need a list of verified emails to load somewhere else, several tools do that well and cheaply. Hunter is the cleanest simple option: type a domain, receive the address pattern and the addresses, verify in the same view. Apollo bundles email finding into a broader platform at a price most teams can absorb. The reason to reach past those is that a raw email is inert. Someone still has to research the account, write something worth reading, send it, and chase the reply. That someone is usually a rep spending 40-60% of the week on non-selling busywork. Artisan's angle is that the finding and the doing live in one system, so the address never sits in a spreadsheet waiting for a human to act on it. Ava also enriches beyond the address itself: verified job title, company signals like funding rounds, new executive hires, and active hiring, and AI web research on the person, all attached before the first message goes out. That is the difference between finding an email and knowing why you are writing to it. What is the best phone number finder for sales? The best phone number finder for sales is Artisan, because mobile coverage is the hardest part of contact data and waterfall enrichment is the honest way to solve it. No single provider has every direct dial. Ava queries roughly a dozen phone data sources in sequence until one returns a verified number, charges only on success, and then makes that number usable inside the dialer, where calls run as steps in the same multichannel sequence as the email and social media touches. On raw phone data alone, two specialists deserve real credit. Cognism's Diamond Data verifies mobile numbers by calling them and scrubs against do-not-call (DNC) and Telephone Preference Service (TPS) lists, which is why compliance-focused teams across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) lean on it. Lusha built its reputation on fast, accurate direct dials pulled from a browser extension while a rep is looking at a prospect. Both are excellent at the narrow job of returning a good number. Where they stop is action: the number lands in your tool, and a rep still has to dial it, log it, and follow up. Artisan closes that gap. Found numbers flow into a dialer with power and parallel dialing across up to three lines, AI answer detection, live transcription, live talking points loaded before the call connects, auto-classified outcomes, native CRM logging, and an AI-drafted follow-up email. Dialer seats and phone numbers are billed separately from Ava's usage-based credits, at $75/seat/month when paid monthly, with one seat per caller and roughly one phone number per 50 calls a day. So the number you found does not just sit in a field. It is dialed, logged to the right rep's CRM record, and followed up on automatically. How we chose Four criteria, weighted for how sales teams actually use this data in 2026. The first is how much of the job the tool does. Finding a contact is step one of a longer motion, so tools that only return data score lower than tools that turn the data into outreach, because the buyer's real problem is pipeline, not a spreadsheet. The second is data and verification depth. Raw database size matters, but verification matters more. A tool claiming 300M profiles with a 25% bounce rate is worse than a smaller, cleaner database. We weighted verified email deliverability and mobile-phone accuracy heavily, and noted where vendor-claimed numbers are self-reported. The third is pricing transparency. Published, per-seat or per-credit pricing beats demo-gated enterprise contracts for most buyers, and we flagged annual-only auto-renewal terms and gated pricing where they exist. The fourth is deployment fit, meaning how the tool sits in a real stack: CRM sync, whether enrichment charges on success or on every attempt, and whether the found data can trigger action without a human copy-pasting it. The best email and phone finder tools, ranked 1. Artisan: The finder that also runs the outreach Artisan is an AI-first outbound platform built around Ava, the autonomous AI business development representative (BDR). On the data side, she searches over 250M B2B professionals in over 200 countries, plus Artisan Local Data with over 250M local businesses, using natural-language search and ideal customer profile (ICP) filters, then runs waterfall enrichment across roughly a dozen providers for both email and phone. Artisan ranks first for a different reason than raw accuracy against Cognism's mobile data or ZoomInfo's US firmographic depth. The found contact immediately becomes work. Ava writes personalized multichannel outreach across email, social media, and dialer calls, runs dozens of message variations and shifts volume toward the ones that convert, handles every reply from a knowledge base, and books meetings on reps' calendars with CRM-owner routing. Sales ops can run her centrally for large account executive teams who never log in, with a full audit trail and plain-language escalation rules. Over 90% of Artisan customers run Ava autonomously. SumUp's growth lead, Karlo Biuk, put the enrichment payoff concretely: the team drove a $52 cost per lead across over 400,000 personalized emails and now receives 8-15 positive replies per week from previously unreachable local small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs). That local-business reach is a genuine gap in most B2B finders, which only index corporate contacts. Best for: teams from startup to enterprise that want found contacts to turn into sent, personalized outreach without a human moving data between tools Who should pick something else: if you only need a raw export of verified emails to feed a tool you already run, a standalone finder like Hunter or Apollo is cheaper for that single job Pricing: usage-based credits for Ava's work, with enrichment charged only on success, plus a free trial. Dialer seats and phone numbers are billed separately at $75/seat/month when paid monthly. See pricing 2. Apollo: The value all-in-one Apollo is the price-accessible default. It claims over 230M contacts, is used by over 600,000 companies (over 100,000 paying), and reportedly passed $200M ARR, with a free tier and paid plans up to around $119/user/month. It bundles email and phone finding with basic sequencing, so a small team can prospect and send from one login. Apollo acquired Pocus in March 2026, adding buyer-intent signals to the data layer. The honest limit is that Apollo's AI assists a rep instead of acting on its own, and it runs on a per-seat model that larger orgs tend to treat as a data source rather than an execution engine. Mobile-phone accuracy is decent but not class-leading. Best for: startups and mid-market teams that want a broad database plus light sequencing at a transparent, low price Who should pick something else: teams that need the outreach run for them, not just the data, or that want the deepest verified mobile coverage for calling Pricing: free tier; paid plans to around $119/user/month per its pricing page 3. ZoomInfo: The enterprise US data standard ZoomInfo remains the reference point for enterprise US data depth. Now repositioned as a go-to-market intelligence platform (ticker $GTM), it claims over 321M profiles (its own figure) and adds Scoops (human-sourced intelligence) and WebSights (visitor identification). Buyer-reported contracts start around $15K/year. For a large team that needs the deepest firmographic and org-chart data in North America, ZoomInfo is still the incumbent. The limits are familiar: it is a data platform first, with execution features layered on as add-ons, and its contract terms have a reputation buyers should go in aware of. Best for: enterprises that need maximum US firmographic and contact depth and have budget for a data platform Who should pick something else: teams that want published pricing, or that care more about the outreach than the raw data, or that prospect heavily in EMEA where Cognism often wins on phones Pricing: demo-gated; roughly $15K/year and up per buyer-reported contracts 4. Cognism: EMEA phone verification and compliance Cognism is the compliance-first choice, strongest in EMEA. Its Diamond Data verifies mobile numbers by phone-checking them, and it scrubs against DNC and TPS lists, which is exactly what teams calling into regulated European markets need. If verified mobile direct dials into Europe are the job, Cognism is the strongest specialist option. Two honest notes: pricing is gated (roughly $15-50K/year reported), and its Kaspr subsidiary was fined 240,000 euros by France's data protection regulator, the CNIL, in December 2024, per public reporting, which is worth knowing for a compliance-led buyer. Best for: EMEA-focused teams that need verified mobile numbers and strict DNC and consent compliance Who should pick something else: US-centric teams (ZoomInfo or Apollo cover North America more deeply), or anyone who wants the data to run its own outreach Pricing: gated; roughly $15-50K/year reported 5. Lusha: Fast direct dials for reps Lusha is built for speed at the individual-rep level. Its browser extension reveals verified emails and mobile numbers while a rep is looking at a prospect's profile, which makes it a favorite for reps who prospect one account at a time. It has a free tier and published per-seat plans, so it is easy to adopt without procurement. The trade-off is that Lusha is a lookup tool, not a system. It returns a good number and stops there; everything after the lookup is manual. Best for: individual reps and small teams that want fast, accurate direct dials on demand Who should pick something else: teams that need bulk enrichment tied to sequencing, or the deepest enterprise database Pricing: free tier plus published per-seat plans per its pricing page 6. Hunter: The simple email specialist Hunter does one thing cleanly: find and verify email addresses by domain. Type a company domain, receive the address pattern and the known emails, verify them in the same view. Its free tier is generous and its API is developer-friendly, which is why it shows up inside a lot of homegrown workflows. Hunter is email-only, with essentially no phone data, and no outreach engine beyond basic campaigns. That focus is the point. Best for: teams that want a straightforward, affordable email finder and verifier, especially via API Who should pick something else: anyone who needs phone numbers, deep firmographics, or the outreach run for them Pricing: free tier; paid plans to around $500/month per its pricing page 7. RocketReach: Broad reach across channels RocketReach casts a wide net, returning emails, phone numbers, and social profiles across a large index of people. Its breadth and API make it useful for filling gaps other tools miss, and its published per-lookup tiers are easy to reason about. Coverage is broad rather than deep, so verification quality varies more than with a specialist like Cognism on phones or Hunter on email. Treat it as a complement. Best for: teams that want broad multi-channel contact coverage and a simple API Who should pick something else: teams that need the highest verification accuracy on a single channel, or an execution layer Pricing: published per-lookup and per-seat tiers 8. Seamless.AI: Real-time search at volume Seamless.AI markets itself as a live search engine for contacts, guessing and verifying emails in real time at high volume. Reps who need a lot of contacts fast sometimes like the throughput. Caveats are worth stating plainly: users report bounce rates in the 20-30% range, the contracts are annual-only with auto-renewal terms, and Seamless was removed from a major professional network in March 2025 over scraping, per public reporting. Go in with eyes open on data quality and terms. Best for: high-volume prospectors who prioritize contact quantity and speed over verification precision Who should pick something else: teams that need clean, low-bounce data, flexible terms, or compliance assurance Pricing: published tiers; annual-only auto-renewal per user reports What actually makes a finder good in 2026? Two things, and neither is database size. First, verification. A vendor claiming over 300M profiles means little if a quarter of the emails bounce or the mobiles are dead. Real-world match and accuracy rates often land well below the headline claims, especially on mobile numbers, where verified direct-dial coverage is the hard problem. Waterfall enrichment (querying multiple providers in sequence and taking the first verified hit) beats any single source, which is why the serious platforms all do it. Charging only on a successful match is the honest version of that model. Second, whether the data moves. The old workflow was: finder returns a list, ops uploads it to a sequencer, a rep writes the emails, someone dials the numbers. Every handoff loses time and data. In 2026 the tools worth paying for collapse those steps. That is the entire reason Artisan ranks a finder-plus-outreach system above pure lookup tools: the found contact should trigger the outreach instead of waiting in a CSV. If you want the mechanics of how an AI runs that full loop, see our explainer on what an AI BDR is . What changed in contact data recently? The market consolidated and repriced. Apollo acquired Pocus in March 2026, folding buyer-intent signals into its data platform. ZoomInfo completed its rebrand to the GTM Intelligence Platform and now trades under $GTM. Clearbit disappeared as a standalone: HubSpot acquired it in December 2023 and sunset it through 2025, with its data now living inside HubSpot as Breeze Intelligence credits. Cognism's Kaspr fine from France's CNIL (December 2024) kept compliance in the headlines for EMEA data buyers. The throughline: raw data is commoditizing, and the value is shifting to verification quality and to what happens after the contact is found. FAQ What is the difference between an email finder and a phone number finder? An email finder returns verified email addresses, usually by matching a name and company domain against a database or guessing the pattern. A phone number finder returns direct dials and mobile numbers, which is harder because verified mobile data is scarcer and decays faster. Many tools do both, but quality diverges: a strong email finder can have weak phone coverage and vice versa. Artisan runs waterfall enrichment across roughly a dozen providers for both, and charges only when it lands a verified result. Which email finder has the lowest bounce rate? Bounce rate depends on verification more than database size. Tools that verify addresses in real time and run waterfall enrichment across multiple sources tend to bounce least. Be cautious with vendors whose users report 20-30% bounce rates. Artisan verifies every email and only charges on a successful match, so you do not pay for addresses that fail. What is the best tool for finding mobile phone numbers? For verified mobile direct dials, Cognism's Diamond Data and Lusha lead among standalone specialists, and Cognism is especially strong in EMEA with DNC and TPS scrubbing. Artisan ranks first overall because it runs waterfall phone enrichment across roughly a dozen providers, charges only on success, and then makes the number dialable inside a sequence rather than leaving it in a field. Is Apollo or ZoomInfo better for contact data? Apollo wins on price and accessibility, with a free tier and plans to around $119/user/month, and works well for startups and mid-market teams. ZoomInfo wins on US enterprise data depth, claiming over 321M profiles with buyer-reported contracts from roughly $15K/year. Pick Apollo for value and self-serve; pick ZoomInfo when maximum North American firmographic depth justifies the price and the demo-gated contract. Does a contact finder replace a sales engagement tool? Traditionally no. A finder returns data, and a separate sequencer or dialer acts on it. That handoff is exactly what slows teams down. The 2026 shift is toward systems where finding and outreach live together, so the contact triggers action automatically. Artisan is built that way: Ava finds and enriches the contact, then writes, sends, and follows up on the outreach in the same platform. Compare the AI sales agent approach to a stitched stack. How much should I pay for contact data? It varies from free tiers up to enterprise contracts north of $15K/year. The number to watch is not the headline price but the cost per verified, usable contact. Pay-on-success enrichment (you are charged only when a valid match is returned) is the fairest model, because you never pay for a bounce or a dead number. Standalone finders that charge per lookup regardless of match quality can cost more per usable record than they appear to. Can these tools find contacts for local businesses, not just corporate? Most B2B finders index corporate contacts only and miss local businesses like restaurants, gyms, and local services. Artisan is unusual in carrying Artisan Local Data, over 250M local businesses, alongside its over 250M B2B professionals, which is why teams selling into local SMBs use it to reach accounts other tools cannot see. SumUp used this reach to generate 8-15 positive replies per week from previously unreachable local SMBs. The bottom line If you just need a clean list of verified emails, Hunter and Apollo are cheap and good, and Cognism and Lusha lead on verified phones, especially in EMEA. But finding the contact is the easy half of the job now. The half that drives pipeline is what happens next, and that is where a system that finds, enriches, writes, sends, and follows up beats a lookup tool that stops at the export. title: McLane: The Distributor Walmart Sold and Still Depends On
summary: McLane Company made the 2025 MDM Top Distributors Food & Beverage list. Here is how a company Walmart sold in 2003 still supplies Walmart's shelves today.
body_text: Part of Distributor Playbooks — strategy teardowns of every company on the 2025 MDM Top Distributors lists . McLane Company shows up on Modern Distribution Management's 2025 Top Distributors list in the Food & Beverage category, one of twenty verticals MDM tracks across North America's largest wholesalers. McLane does not disclose revenue the way most companies on that list do, because it has not been an independent company since 2003. It is a Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary, and it is the supply line behind a huge share of the snacks, drinks, and fresh food sold at convenience stores and restaurants across the country. A grocery store that became a warehouse The company started in 1894, when Robert McLane opened a retail grocery in Cameron, Texas. By 1903 the family had flipped the model: instead of selling groceries to shoppers, they sold groceries to other grocers, shipping by rail and horse-drawn wagon around Central Texas. That inversion, retailer to wholesaler, is the same move the company has been running for 130 years, just at a scale Robert McLane could not have imagined. The company moved to Temple, Texas in 1966 and, under Drayton McLane Jr. starting in 1976, expanded outward from grocery into the convenience store channel that was then exploding across the country. By 1990 McLane had a genuinely national footprint. That was also the year Drayton McLane sold the company to Walmart, for 10.4 million shares of Walmart stock plus cash, according to Wikipedia's account of the company's history . The sale that didn't end the relationship Here is the detail that makes McLane worth studying rather than just noting: Walmart owned McLane for barely a decade, selling it to Berkshire Hathaway in May 2003 for $1.45 billion. But Walmart didn't stop being McLane's customer when it stopped being McLane's owner. Walmart and Sam's Club remained McLane's largest client relationship afterward, accounting for roughly a quarter of McLane's revenue as of the mid-2010s. That is the unusual part of McLane's model: it is a captive supply chain that outlived its captivity. Most distributors either serve one dominant retail parent or serve nobody in particular. McLane did both, in sequence, and the divestiture didn't sever the dependency in either direction. Walmart still needed a distributor that knew its stores cold; McLane still needed the volume. Berkshire got a business with a built-in anchor customer it never had to negotiate into existence. Building out from grocery into three businesses Once independent of Walmart's balance sheet, McLane spent the 2000s and 2010s stacking categories onto its core grocery wholesale business rather than chasing new geography. The acquisitions tell the story of a company deliberately becoming three companies in one: Year Acquisition What it added 2000 AmeriServe Food Distribution assets Foundation for McLane Foodservice, entry into restaurant chain supply 2004 C.D. Hartnett Texas grocery wholesale density 2006 McCarty-Hull Amarillo-market grocery reach 2010 Empire Distributors Southeast beverage distribution 2012 Meadowbrook Meat Company National foodservice protein distribution The result, per the company's own account, is a network of more than 80 grocery and foodservice distribution centers (plus one in Brazil) moving over 10 billion pounds of merchandise a year to roughly 110,000 locations, using a fleet that includes more than 6,100 multi-temperature trailers, according to McLane's own site . That multi-temp fleet detail matters more than it sounds: running frozen, refrigerated, and dry goods through the same truck and the same route is the actual engineering problem of foodservice distribution, and it's the reason grocery wholesalers and restaurant suppliers rarely cross into each other's lanes successfully. McLane built the capability to do both under one logistics network instead of running them as separate businesses that happen to share a logo. Thin margins, enormous volume, quiet ownership McLane's economics are the least glamorous part of the story and the most instructive. Distribution at this scale runs on volume, not markup. It is not the kind of business Berkshire is known for buying, no brand moat, no pricing power, no consumer mindshare. Buffett doesn't talk about McLane in shareholder letters the way he talks about See's Candy or GEICO, because there isn't a charming story to tell about trailer utilization rates. What McLane offers instead is dependable, unglamorous cash generation from a network that would be brutally expensive for a new entrant to replicate. That is a moat built entirely out of physical infrastructure and route density, which is a less quotable answer but a real one. Where the next chapter is being written The clearest signal of where McLane is placing bets right now is a May 2026 partnership with Aurora to pilot autonomous trucks on restaurant-supply-chain routes in Texas, moving from supervised pilots toward driverless long-haul runs. It is a fitting bookend: a company that started with horse-drawn wagons in 1894 is now testing trucks with nobody in the cab, on the same basic promise, get the product to the store reliably and cheaply. McLane is also leaning into supplier-facing programming, its McLane Engage conference returns in August 2026 with an AI-focused keynote, suggesting the next competitive fight in wholesale distribution is as much about who owns the data and automation layer as who owns the trucks. None of this shows up on a receipt. The convenience store shelf, the restaurant walk-in cooler, the vending machine, all of it depends on a catalog, a route plan, and a truck showing up on time, which is the quiet infrastructure this series keeps coming back to.

title: How to Transfer a Car Title to a Family Member
summary: How do you transfer a car title to a family member? Our jargon-free guide walks you through the process in simple steps.
body_text: Whether it’s a grandparent gifting a car to a grandchild, an older brother passing their car on to a younger sibling or parents gifting an old family runabout to their offspring, title transfers to family members is a common occurrence. They can also come up during estate settlements. The title transfer process might seem complex but it’s actually quite straightforward: fill out the title paperwork and Bob’s your uncle (or parent or grandfather, as the case may be). There are potential catches and pitfalls, however, and there may be sales tax and registration fees to be aware of. Here, we’ll aim to cut through the jargon and make the whole thing as simple and fuss-free as possible. How to Transfer a Car Title to a Family Member What Is a Title? What Vehicles Need a Title? What if I’m Missing a Title? What if I Never Received a Title When I Bought My Car? How Do I Transfer a Title? Do I Need a Title Notarized? Can I Avoid Paying Sales Tax if the Vehicle Transfer is from a Family Member? What if the Vehicle I Received Was a Gift? Can I Avoid Paying Registration Fees When Transferring a Title to a Family Member? What Is a Title? A certificate of title is the piece of paperwork that proves ownership of a vehicle and provides key vehicle information. For at least the past 50 years, whenever you purchase a new car from a dealership or other retailer, that retailer provides the department of motor vehicles (DMV) in your state with a Manufacturer Statement of Origin (MSO). The MSO shows that the vehicle is new, with its corresponding vehicle identification number (VIN), and that the manufacturer is transferring ownership of that new vehicle to you, the buyer. From that point on, all 50 states require that a new owner fills out a title application every time a vehicle transfers ownership. Once you’ve filled out the title application, your state's Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) will process the paperwork and eventually send you a physical vehicle title on watermarked paper for your records. When you sell your vehicle, you'll fill out the appropriate section of the title (often on the back of the title), and then the next buyer will use that to establish the chain of car ownership, again applying for their own title to help prove ownership of the vehicle, which they’ll eventually get in the mail. Tero Vesalainen/iStock via Getty Images What Vehicles Need a Title? Again, determining which vehicles need a title is state-specific. Most states—41, in fact—require a title for ALL vehicles, regardless of year. The nine remaining states have varying requirements: Alabama: 1980 and newer Connecticut: 20 years old and newer Georgia: 1986 and newer Maine: 1995 and newer Massachusetts: 1990 and newer New Hampshire: 15 years old and newer New York: 1973 and newer Rhode Island: 2001 and newer Vermont: 15 years old and newer In those states that don’t require a title for older vehicles, other legal documents such as a bill of sale and the current vehicle registration typically suffice for proof of ownership. What if I’m Missing a Title? All states have a duplicate title process if you find that your original title has gone missing. If you’re from one of the nine states above, check to be sure that your vehicle needs a title at all. If it does, you’ll need to visit your state’s DMV or Department of Revenue to fill out the duplicate title paperwork and pay the appropriate fee. Be aware that a duplicate title may take several weeks to process. Tero Vesalainen/iStock via Getty Images What if I Never Received a Title When I Bought My Car? If you never received a title from your department of motor vehicles, it's most likely because you have a lien on the vehicle. If you took out a loan to pay for the car, then in 41 states, known as "title-holding states," the DMV sends the title to the lienholder. Once you've paid the vehicle off in full, the lienholder sends the title to you. There are nine "non-title-holding states:" Arizona Kentucky Maryland Michigan Minnesota New York Oklahoma South Dakota Wisconsin In those nine states, the title comes directly to you regardless of whether there's an outstanding loan on the vehicle. However, the title will be in both the owner’s name and the lender's. Once you pay the vehicle off in full, you'll receive a Release of Lien letter. This lien release then allows you to apply for a title in just your name. How Do I Transfer a Title? Vehicle title transfers are simple, but the transfer process can be highly specific. States can be absurdly stringent about any kind of marks, missing data, or information filled out incorrectly, or in the wrong place on a vehicle title. There was a time when the Commonwealth of Massachusetts would reject a vehicle title if it had staple holes in it, for example. States usually provide warnings for filling out the title, like Kentucky's: “Warning: Do not use liquid paper/Wite-Out on your title. Do not scratch through or mark out information on the title. Do not erase or mutilate.” When you’re transferring any title—whether it’s to a family member or otherwise—be sure to read the instructions on the title carefully, and only print, sign, and fill out the odometer reading where you’re supposed to. Some states such as Texas, Utah, and California offer partial online services for transferring titles, but in general this is something that needs to be done in person. Tero Vesalainen/iStock via Getty Images Do I Need a Title Notarized? 42 states allow vehicle owners to sign over the title and submit the paperwork to the local DMV office or Department of Revenue without any oversight. In the following eight states, do not sign the title or fill out any of the fields until you are in the presence of a notary public: Arizona Kentucky Louisiana Montana North Carolina Ohio Oklahoma Pennsylvania If you live in one of these states, you must sign your title in front of a notary, providing your driver’s license number or valid ID. The notary witnesses the signature and provides a notary stamp on the title. Most local banks, UPS stores, and law firms have a notary on staff, as do some insurance agencies. Can I Avoid Paying Sales Tax if the Vehicle Transfer is from a Family Member? As far as all 50 states are concerned, transferring a title to a family member is no different than if you were to transfer ownership to anyone else. If the vehicle is going to be housed in another location and registered by another person, that person needs to receive a signed title filled out by the previous owner and then needs to submit it, along with an application for a new title and the requisite title transfer fee. Where things get interesting is whether or not states require sales tax to be paid between family members. Five states—Alaska, Delaware, Montana, New Hampshire, and Oregon—have no sales tax. In 45 other states, sales tax is expected to be paid every time a vehicle changes hands. Almost every state at this point collects sales tax based on a “blue book value” or fair market value, rather than on the actual purchase price you paid. Any potential sales tax exemptions are specific to your state’s laws. We’ll use Massachusetts as an example: In the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you can avoid paying sales tax on a vehicle if it’s transferred from one of the following: Father/Mother Brother/Sister Husband/Wife Son/Daughter The family member transferring the vehicle must fill out Form MVU-26, Affidavit in Support of a Claim for Exemption from Sales or Use Tax for a Motor Vehicle Transferred Within a Family. Other states offer similar methods of avoiding sales tax through the transfer from an immediate family member. Prostock-Studio/iStock via Getty Images What if the Vehicle I Received Was a Gift? There are also provisions that allow the transfer of title avoiding sales tax by gifting the vehicle to a new owner. This doesn't necessarily have to be a family member; for example, a vehicle can be "gifted" if someone's done work on your house and they agreed to take your 1971 Nova as payment instead of cash. The Tennessee Department of Revenue offers an Affidavit of Non-Dealer Transfers of Motor Vehicles and Boats (Form RV-F1301201). That form allows the transferee to declare that the vehicle was either given as a gift or sold for a low selling price, with a space for the transferee to declare the reason for the sale price. Can I Avoid Paying Registration Fees When Transferring a Title to a Family Member? In general, no. Registration fees are assessed whenever a new license plate is issued. If you're acquiring a vehicle from a family member, you must go through the process to acquire a new registration, even if you received your new car through a gift transfer. There are some specific circumstances that may allow you to keep a family member's license plate number. In Massachusetts, for example, low number license plates have been passed from family member to family member for generations. Massachusetts has a specific process for making that transfer, which usually requires a death certificate but still requires a nominal license plate transfer fee. (Nasdaq: RCAT) (“Red Cat” or the “Company”), a U.S.-based provider of advanced all-domain drone and robotic solutions for defense and national security, today announced that it has completed integration work with C3A Solutions (“C3A”) to connect Red Cat’s Black Widow™ small unmanned aircraft system with OBERON-enabled tactical fires networks. C3A is a tactical systems integration company specializing in digital fires, tactical communications, and operational network integration for Army units at the tactical edge. This is where small unmanned systems are headed, and where we believe Red Cat can play a critical role for the warfighter.” C3A’s tactical integration portfolio includes support for fire control systems, operational targeting systems, precision fires platforms, tactical radios, laser designators, positioning, navigation and timing devices, and unmanned aerial vehicles. The company’s materials identify Black Widow and OBERON integration across fires and tactical networks as part of its unmanned aerial vehicle integration capabilities. “C3A’s strength is translating emerging technology into field-ready capability,” said Dan Morgan, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of C3A Solutions. “Our work with Red Cat helps ensure Black Widow can integrate into the digital fires environment in a way that is practical for soldiers and useful to commanders. By connecting sensors, radios and fires systems in the field, we can help units reduce friction, move information with greater confidence, and keep pace with the speed of modern operations.” The collaboration reflects Red Cat’s continued focus on interoperability and mission-driven integration across its Family of Systems. By working with field-focused integration partners like C3A, Red Cat is helping ensure its systems can connect into existing and emerging tactical architectures used by military customers. title: Mem0 Claude Connector: Persistent Memory Across Every Chat
summary: Mem0 is now an official Anthropic connector for Claude. No CLI or config file needed. Just search, connect, and Claude remembers every chat.
body_text: Claude can already remember things between chats. Its built-in memory carries some context forward from one conversation to the next. But that memory lives inside Claude- it doesn't follow you to your IDE, your own agents, or any other tool, and you don't control what's stored or how. Mem0 gives you a portable, persistent, long-term memory that works across your chat sessions and the tools you build on. Introducing the Mem0 Connector for Claude, now listed in Anthropic's official Connectors Directory. Search for Mem0, connect it from claude.ai , Claude Desktop, or Cowork, and every chat has persistent memory. Fig: Mem0 Claude connector listed in Anthropic's Connectors Directory What changes! Nothing about how Mem0 stores or retrieves memories has changed. What's new is how you reach it: no more CLI, just a connector you click into from claude.ai , Desktop, or Cowork. Here's what that unlocks: No install path: The connector runs on Mem0's hosted MCP server ( mcp.mem0.ai/mcp ). No local setup required. Available everywhere within Claude: It works identically across Claude.ai , Claude Desktop, and Cowork. The CLI plugin already covered Claude Code and the API. This connector closes the gap for everyone else. Eleven memory tools(callable in plain English): This connector consists of 11 memory tools, including add_memory , search_memories , get_memories , get_memory , update_memory , delete_memory , delete_all_memories , list_entities , and three more. Claude decides on its own when a tool applies. One setup prompt: The connector ships a memory_assistant prompt that gives Claude a quick start on how to use the tools. No SDK changes: Existing add() and search() calls in your own Mem0 integrations are untouched. How it works? Adding this Claude connector authorizes Claude to call Mem0's hosted MCP server on your behalf(scoped to your Mem0 account). Memories are scoped per user, agent, or session, same isolation model as the API and SDK. Once connected, Claude can store facts from a conversation, pull them back in a later one, update a fact that's changed, or delete one you no longer want kept. All of it happens server-side. You never see a tool call unless you ask Claude to show its work. Getting reliable recall Claude decides per-turn whether a query is worth a memory lookup. Under Auto tool access (the default), a casual, low-signal question may not trigger a search. Two ways to make retrieval reliable: Name the action: "check my Mem0 memory for X" instead of a vague ask. Switch Mem0's tool access to Always available in Connectors → Tool access , so it's loaded into context on every turn instead of fetched only when Claude judges it relevant. Setup Open the "+" button or type / , then go to Connectors. Search " Mem0 " in the Directory and click Connect. Authorize with your Mem0 account. Start a new chat and ask Claude to save or recall something explicitly the first time, to confirm the connection works end-to-end. Applications Coding assistants: Project conventions, architecture decisions, and debugging history carry over automatically, without any CLAUDE.md rules or re-explaining. Support and research workflows: Customer history and research context accumulate across weeks of conversations instead of resetting every time. Personal use: Preferences set in one chat show up in the next, without needing a project or an app-specific memory feature.

body_text: A widely used allergy medication has been recalled after concerns were raised about possible contamination during manufacturing. Consumers who use allergy tablets are being advised to check their medicine supplies and stay informed about the latest safety updates. The recall involves certain batches of cetirizine hydrochloride tablets, a commonly used antihistamine medication that helps relieve symptoms linked to seasonal allergies and hives. The recall was announced after a possible cross-contamination issue was identified, creating concerns for people who may have sensitivity to another ingredient. Why Have the Allergy Tablets Been Recalled? The pharmaceutical company Rising Pharma Holdings Inc. announced the recall of specific lots of 5 milligram cetirizine hydrochloride tablets. The medication was manufactured by Unique Pharmaceutical Laboratories, a company based in India, and distributed across the United States. According to safety information released by the companies and health authorities, some tablets may have been unintentionally contaminated with traces of ranitidine. Ranitidine is a medication that was previously used to reduce stomach acid and treat conditions such as acid reflux and indigestion. The concern is not that cetirizine itself is unsafe when used correctly. The issue relates specifically to the possibility that some tablets may contain another substance because of a manufacturing problem. Details of the Recalled Medication Consumers should carefully check whether their allergy tablets match the recalled product information. The recalled medicine includes: • Medication: Cetirizine hydrochloride tablets, 5 milligrams • Package size: Bottles containing 100 tablets • Manufacturer: Unique Pharmaceutical Laboratories, a division of J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals Ltd. • Distributor: Rising Pharma Holdings Inc. • National Drug Code: 16571-401-10 • Expiration date: October 2028 The affected lot numbers include: • GY825029 • GY825030 • GY825031 • GY825032 Anyone who has these products should avoid using them until they receive further guidance from a healthcare professional or the manufacturer. Possible Health Concerns At the time of the recall announcement, no adverse reactions had been reported from people taking the affected tablets. However, officials warned that individuals who have a sensitivity to ranitidine ingredients could potentially experience serious reactions. A severe allergic reaction, known as anaphylaxis, can require urgent medical attention. Symptoms may include difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, dizziness, rapid heartbeat, or a sudden drop in blood pressure. People who experience unusual symptoms after taking medication should seek medical advice immediately. What Should Customers Do? Consumers who have purchased cetirizine hydrochloride tablets should check the bottle label and compare the information with the recall details. If the medicine matches the recalled batches, customers should: • Stop using the affected tablets • Contact their pharmacist or healthcare provider for advice • Follow official instructions regarding disposal or replacement • Report any possible side effects or reactions People should not stop necessary allergy treatment without speaking to a medical professional, especially if they rely on antihistamines to manage ongoing symptoms. Why Medication Recalls Matter Medicine recalls are issued when manufacturers or regulators identify a potential safety concern. These actions are designed to protect consumers and prevent possible harm. Manufacturing mistakes can happen for several reasons, including equipment problems, packaging errors, contamination risks, or quality control issues. Pharmaceutical companies are required to follow strict safety procedures, but recalls can still occur when unexpected problems are discovered. A recall does not always mean that every product is dangerous. Instead, it means certain batches need to be removed from circulation while the issue is investigated. How Consumers Can Stay Safe Keeping track of medication information can help consumers respond quickly when safety alerts are announced. Useful steps include: • Keep medicines in their original packaging • Check expiry dates regularly • Stay updated through official health websites • Ask pharmacists about replacement options • Report unusual reactions after taking medicines Consumers should avoid relying only on social media posts or unofficial reports for medical information. Government health agencies, pharmacists, and healthcare providers remain the most reliable sources for medication safety updates. Importance of Speaking With Healthcare Professionals People who regularly use allergy medication may have questions about alternative treatments after a recall. A doctor or pharmacist can recommend suitable options based on individual health needs. Different allergy medicines work in different ways, and replacing medication without professional advice may not always be appropriate. Patients with a history of severe allergies or reactions to medicines should be especially careful and discuss concerns with a qualified healthcare provider. Final Thoughts The recall of certain cetirizine hydrochloride tablets highlights the importance of medication safety awareness. While no adverse reactions had been reported at the time of the announcement, consumers are encouraged to check their products and follow official guidance. Staying informed, checking medicine labels, and communicating with healthcare professionals can help people make safer decisions about their health. Readers should consult a doctor, pharmacist, or qualified healthcare provider regarding medication concerns, possible side effects, or treatment decisions. Always check official health authority announcements for the latest recall information.

Según un estudio de Zebra Technologies, existe actualmente una necesidad por conocer el origen y el nivel de sostenibilidad de los materiales y las piezas de automóviles, así como de tener una visión integral del proceso de fabricación. LATAM, 02 de mayo 2023.- El sector automotriz está experimentando un cambio radical en los últimos años. Esto se debe principalmente a la transformación digital, la aceleración de la tecnología y el uso de herramientas avanzadas como Inteligencia Artificial/Machine Learning (IA/ML), o el Internet de las Cosas (IoT). Estas tendencias están cambiando el modo en que se fabrican los vehículos y conducen al desarrollo de nuevas soluciones para mejorar la productividad y reducir los costos. En este 2023, las tendencias de fabricación en el sector automotriz incluirán la aceleración en la automatización, así como la convergencia entre la Tecnología de Información (TI) y IoT. Zebra Technologies Corporation , empresa innovadora en la primera línea de los negocios con soluciones y socios que ofrecen una ventaja de rendimiento, publicó los resultados de su estudio Automotive Ecosystem Vision Study , que confirma que los fabricantes de automóviles están bajo presión para satisfacer las crecientes demandas de los consumidores entorno a la sostenibilidad y transparencia en todo el proceso de fabricación, así como la necesidad de los gestores de flotas de digitalizar las operaciones y la cadena de suministro. A pesar de una economía en constante cambio, los fabricantes de automóviles están dispuestos a invertir en innovación tecnológica, pues uno de los hallazgos del estudio muestra que siete de cada diez esperan aumentar su gasto en tecnología y seis de cada diez planean aumentar su gasto en infraestructura de fabricación en 2023. Los consumidores son una fuerza impulsora detrás de la aceleración de los fabricantes de automóviles hacia la innovación tecnológica, ya que ocho de cada diez dicen que la sostenibilidad y el respeto al medio ambiente son prioridades clave en sus decisiones de compra y arrendamiento de vehículos. El 71% de los Millennials dan prioridad a la sostenibilidad en sus vehículos, seguidos de cerca del 79% de los pertenecientes a los Gen X y el 82% de los Baby Boomers. Los consumidores han incrementado su interés por la personalización; es decir, la posibilidad de adaptar un vehículo a su gusto. Casi cuatro de cada cinco consumidores afirman que las opciones de personalización influyen en su decisión de compra de un vehículo, y casi nueve de cada diez gestores de flotas comparten estos mismos requisitos de sostenibilidad y personalización. Aunque el 72% de los fabricantes de automóviles reconoce que los consumidores esperan más opciones de vehículos sostenibles y personalizados, seis de cada diez admiten que es difícil seguir el ritmo de las crecientes demandas de personalización. Como resultado, tres cuartas partes de los fabricantes de automóviles afirman que una de sus principales prioridades es establecer asociaciones estratégicas con empresas tecnológicas para su próxima generación de producción. "No hay duda de que el ecosistema de fabricación de automóviles está experimentando un cambio drástico con enormes obstáculos que superar. Esto incluye esencialmente la ejecución de dos procesos de fabricación distintos: uno para los vehículos tradicionales de gasolina o diesel y el otro para la próxima generación de vehículos eléctricos, híbridos y autónomos" , mencionó Ana Laura Cacogui, Gerente de Mercadeo para manufactura en Latinoamérica de Zebra Technologies. Los resultados de la encuesta también revelan una mayor preferencia por la compra de vehículos eléctricos (VE) en el futuro, ya que el 61% de los consumidores indican que su preferencia futura es un vehículo eléctrico híbrido (VEH). Sin embargo, este aumento de la demanda de VE conlleva una serie de retos, ya que el 71% de los responsables de la industria automovilística afirma estar sometido a una gran presión para producir vehículos de nueva generación (es decir, eléctricos) y el 76% de ellos se siente presionado para ofrecer productos más ecológicos, sostenibles y seguros para el medio ambiente. Confianza y transparencia en la fabricación de automóviles La transparencia de los datos y la información es muy importante tanto para los consumidores como para los gestores de flotas que buscan una mayor visibilidad del ecosistema automovilístico. Al considerar la compra o el alquiler de un vehículo, el 89% de los consumidores y el 85% de los gestores de flotas indican que quieren conocer el origen de los materiales y las piezas de su vehículo. Igualmente, el 88% de los consumidores latinos, expresan preocupación por el uso de los datos recopilados en sus vehículos. Los Millennials lideran el camino hacia una mayor transparencia en la fabricación de automóviles, ya que ocho de cada diez señalan que es importante tener acceso a la información del fabricante, además de saber si los materiales de origen y las piezas generan un menor impacto para el medio ambiente. De igual forma, manifiestan su deseo de comprender cómo se fabrica el vehículo de principio a fin. Visibilidad de la cadena de suministro de la industria automovilística La mayoría de los consumidores y gestores de flotas (80%) desean visibilidad de extremo a extremo durante el proceso de fabricación. Sin embargo, sólo el 28% de los responsables de la industria automotriz afirman que darán prioridad a la conexión de sistemas de datos en tiempo real para obtener una visión completa de las operaciones y mejorar la visibilidad de la producción y de toda la cadena de suministro en los próximos cinco años. Alrededor de un tercio de los fabricantes de equipos originales (OEM) afirman que los robots móviles autónomos (AMR), RFID, computadores móviles de mano y escáneres robustos, así como la visión artificial industrial, mejorarán la gestión de la cadena de suministro, mientras que más de un tercio de los proveedores citan las impresoras térmicas/de etiquetas de códigos de barras móviles, los ordenadores portátiles y la tecnología de localización como las tecnologías que lograrán esta gestión. En general, siete de cada diez responsables de la industria del automóvil coinciden en que la transformación digital es una prioridad estratégica para su organización. En los próximos cinco años, prevén ampliar su uso de la tecnología con un 48% centrado en la fabricación aditiva/impresión 3D y un 37% en soluciones de planificación de la cadena de suministro. title: What is a Microschool and How Do I Start One in Arizona?
summary: A detailed walkthrough of how you (yes, you!) can start a microschool (now!) in Arizona.
body_text: Microschools are shaking up the education world in the best way possible! 🎉 These small, community-based schools prioritize personalized learning, flexible pacing, and student empowerment—giving kids an education that actually fits their needs. Unlike traditional schools, microschools offer a more dynamic, hands-on approach where kids can thrive socially and academically. Microschools are growing fast, and Prenda is at the forefront of this movement! As one of the nation’s largest and most trusted microschool networks, Prenda makes it easy and fun to start your own microschool whether you have a professional education background or not (teachers, homeschool mamas, and public school parents- you’re perfect, let’s do this!). While you can absolutely start a microschool independently, it’s a lot harder to do on your own. That’s why we built Prenda—to get all the tricky stuff out. of. your. way. So you can focus on creating a rigorous, yet whimsical , learning environment. 🤯Yes, it’s possible. This guide will walk you through Prenda’s simple 10-step process for launching a microschool in Arizona—plus, we’ll cover Arizona’s Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) program so your students can pay your microschool feels with little to no out-of-pocket cost. Yay! So grab your favorite snack, take a deep breath, and let’s dive into how you can start your microschool adventure in Arizona! It’s going to be amazing. You’re going to be amazing. 🚀 ‍ Step 1: Get Informed and Determine Your Vision You're already doing step 1! 🎉 Reading up on microschools in your area is essential. We recommend checking out these informative articles: What Are Microschools? (EdChoice) What’s a Microschool and Why Focusing on how Kids Learn is Changing Education. (Stand Together) The Rise of Millennial-Powered Microschools (Getting Smart) Consider your "why" and what type of learning environment you want to create. A significant part of this decision is your educational pedagogy and approach. At Prenda, we believe in empowering students to become self-directed learners who have strong skills and an intrinsic drive to pursue their goals. That said, there are many wonderful and beautiful ways to approach educating children. If Prenda's learning approach doesn't match your vision, that's completely okay! We want the future to be full of diverse educational options that meet everyone's unique needs. So even if you want to go it alone, we hope this process overview is a support to you in your journey! 🧳 Step 2: Set Up Your Microschool To get started, simply click " Start My Microschool " on prenda.com (or open that there link in a new tab…go on now, you got this). Starting this process in no way commits you to starting a microschool IRL. You can explore this whole idea with no commitment and no cost. You’ve got nothing to lose! After you click Start My Microschool, you'll be asked some get-to-know-you questions to help tailor the process to your needs. Follow the prompts to create and account and don’t forget to verify your email. Make sure you use the email address you want for all your Prenda communications and microschool business correspondence. Check your email and verify your account. Easy peasy! 📧 Step 3: Choose Who You Want to Serve Will you open your school to other people's children (the norm), or do you want to start with just your own kids in more of a homeschool setting with Prenda's support? This decision will shape your microschool's structure and growth potential. If you just want to homeschool with Prenda, select "Single-family Microschool," and welcome aboard! But if you want to earn an income as a microschool guide in your community, you’ll select the “Multi-family Microschool” option. Step 4: Select Your Funding Source In Arizona, you have two primary funding options: direct pay or the Arizona Empowerment Scholarship Program (ESA). The ESA program works by redirecting state education dollars to parents, allowing them to decide what type of education works best for their student. The average award amount varies depending on your school district but is approximately $7,000 per student per year. Prenda acts as the vendor and manages all the invoicing and payment collection, so guides (that's what we call our microschool teachers!) don't have to worry about it. All K-12 students in Arizona are eligible for this scholarship, and funding is universally given to anyone who applies. This makes Arizona one of the most microschool-friendly states in the country! 🌵 For more detailed information about Arizona's ESA program, check out: Arizona's Empowerment Scholarship Account Program: Everything you need to know Arizona ESA Details Documentation Step 5: Paperwork and Safety Check At this stage you'll sign something called the "Prenda Platform Agreement." 📜 This is a simple agreement between you and Prenda that just describes the relationship between Prenda and anyone using our products and services—stuff like intellectual property use. You should know that when you use Prenda to power your microschool, you are not an employee or independent contractor. You own and operate your own independent microschool and choose to utilize Prenda's services to assist you. Signing the Prenda Platform Agreement does not commit you to running a microschool. After you sign the agreement, you'll initiate a background check for you and for any other adults that will be present during school hours. Prenda handles all the logistics and the expense of providing background checks, all you have to do is fill out your information which takes about 2 minutes. ✅ Step 6: Find a Location and Decide How Much You Will Charge As a microschool founder, you're responsible for finding your own location. The location needs to be safe for kids and have internet access. Think about creating an environment where kids can feel comfortable, be creative, and play. Many Prenda microschools operate out of homes, giving them an intimate, cozy vibe. Others use dance studios, tutoring centers, or even barns and outdoor spaces! 🏡 Here are just a few of the locations where people have run Prenda microschools... Locations Slideshow by Marketing & Media Once you have a location, it's time to decide what your income will be. Prenda guides set their own per-student rate, allowing each microschool founder to control their income. This "guide fee" is typically around $4,000 per student in Arizona. In addition, Prenda charges a $2,199 per-student fee, bringing the total cost for families to about $6,200 per year. 😳 While this may seem high, it's actually much less than public school per student spending, private school tuition, and other child-focused services like daycare. Plus, 99% of Prenda students use state-funded school choice scholarships, covering the cost entirely. Check out Prenda's income calculator to see how much you could earn as a microschool guide. Is Prenda worth the money? YES! We provide comprehensive training, one-on-one coaching, and access to a supportive guide community—all at no upfront cost. Our package includes K-8th curriculum for all subjects, academic coaching, and a microschool management system that makes running your school so easy. We even handle invoicing and payment collection, so you can focus on creating an exceptional learning environment. And instead of nickel and diming you with start up fees, service charges, and coaching expenses, we provide all our services with no upfront cost to you. All of our service fees are baked into that per student Prenda fee, so we only make money when you successfully launch your microschool. Pretty sweet deal, eh? We’re in your corner, no matter what. 🚩 Check out our Curriculum Overview and Guide Toolkit for a deeper dive into what you get. Step 7: Build Your Microschool Profile and Start Outreach Once you have a location and your guide fee is set, you can use Prenda's profile builder to create your microschool profile. This profile gets linked to Prenda's microschool marketplace, which is a map of all the microschools. This makes it easy for prospective parents to find you! You can also use your profile link to text to friends or post on social media. Check out the map of existing microschools here: Find a Microschool As you find interested families, all you have to do is send them an invite to join your school. They'll fill out a quick form, and bam—you'll see them pop up in your Prenda account, ready for school! Step 8: Prenda Guide Certification Training This step-by-step training will teach you more about Prenda's learning system and how kids will learn at your microschool. You'll also get sample schedules and a detailed checklist of things to help prepare you and your students for a successful year. This information will equip you to talk to parents and grow your school. 📚 At Prenda, we provide a research-aligned learning approach that allows every student to progress at their own pace without creating detrimental academic learning gaps or limiting beliefs about themselves as learners. Learning at Prenda is hands-on and focused on building real-world skills and academic mastery. 💡It's rigorous, but fun! Step 9: Your Kick-off Party Hold a school kick-off party with new students and families to get to know each other. Prenda provides details on how to run a successful school kick-off and orientation party so everyone is set up and ready for the first day. 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Creating a sense of belonging from day one sets the tone for a thriving microschool community. Step 10: Start School! What an exciting day this will be! 🎊 Microschool life is truly magical—kids get to be kids while still learning the skills they need to prepare them for the world, all without losing their love of learning. You get to watch them grow, inspire them, coach them, and cheer them on. The Prenda team will continue to support you year-round. If you have any questions or run into any issues, both our team and our guide community are here to help. You’re never alone. ‍ Want to learn more about how this all works? Drop your email to get immediate access to our free overview webinar "Microschooling 101." And if you want to hear the story of Prenda's founding and get a better sense of how the microschooling movement is revolutionizing education, check out this video... ‍
